angle: buyer and program side: MARAD Small Shipyard Grant recipients FY2023-FY2026, Shipbuilders Council of America CY25 safety-award member yards, HII/Electric Boat distributed-shipbuilding and submarine industrial base partners, Navy (YRBM, LSM, MUSV), Coast Guard (WCC, OPC, ASC), Army Corps (dredge, towboat, barge) awards, WorkBoat/Marine Log/Waterways Journal/Riviera construction and delivery coverage, Shipbuilding History active small-builder list
notes: 58 WebSearch queries in total. The last search that produced a new plant was search 49 (dredge builders: DSC Dredge, Ellicott, AmFELS). Searches 50-57 (LPD 32 partners, EB subcontracts, NAVSEA service-craft MAC, Ohio River barges, Alaska, Small Shipyard Grant Coalition, Texas barges, Florida yards) found no new plants. Search 58 only classified two grant recipients that had no row yet (Stevens Towing, Georgetown Shipyard). In-angle sources were then read without new searches (MarineLink 'US Boatbuilding Gains Steam', SCA board page, WorkBoat 2025 Construction Survey pages). They added no new yards: the survey itself is a gated download and could not be read. Quote checking: quotes were checked against the page text printed by tools/fetch_page.py, using the same normalisation as its --check (case, whitespace and quote marks ignored). A spot-check of 6 random rows with live --check returned FOUND for all 6. Weak-evidence rows: 19 in-definition rows rest only on the Shipbuilding History 'Group B - other active builders' table (navalmarinearchive.com/sbh/shipyards/small.html; per-yard pages revised April 2023). For these, neither current (2024-26) activity nor steel construction is confirmed, so compute the miss rate with and without them: Hope Services; Bourg Dry Dock; Duckworth Steel Boats; Inland Boat Works; Jemison Marine & Shipbuilding; Marine Inland Fabricators (Sisco Marine); Midship Marine; Mobro Marine; Newton Boats; Rodriguez Boatbuilding (Coden); Rodriguez Boatbuilding (Bayou La Batre); SanJac Marine; Sneed Shipbuilding; Thoma-Sea Marine Lockport (search 21 found nothing current for it, so it is the weakest); West Gulf Marine; Williams Fabrication; Vessel Repair Port Arthur; Progressive Industrial; Moe Enterprises. Other rows rest on old evidence: Master Marine (2018 article) and BWXT Mount Vernon (2017 page). Grant-list-only out rows are classed repair-only from the grant purpose plus the absence of any new-construction evidence. Possible overlaps left unresolved: Galliano Marine Services MUSV (Houma) may be a Chouest yard already listed (LaShip, Houma); TAI Holdings (Pensacola contractor, place of performance Bayou La Batre) is probably one of the listed Bayou La Batre yards; Steiner Shipyard and Steiner Construction are listed separately, and Riviera and WorkBoat credit the same towboat (Grant Gattle) to different ones of them. Gulf Craft Franklin was merged into Saronic Franklin, since Saronic acquired Gulf Craft. Not placed: HII names Trident Maritime Systems (MI/VA/LA) as a CVN/DDG unit builder, but no plant location was found, so it has no row. Keel's Michigan sites (Saginaw x4, Merrill, Alma) are one row because the welding site is not identified. Sources that failed: the SCA member directory (shipbuildersusa.org/find-a-member) renders names as logos, so the SCA CY25 safety-award list and board page were used instead. maritime.dot.gov, transportation.gov, news.usni.org, gdeb.com, gdbiw.com, hanwhaphilly.com, thomasea.com and navy.mil were blocked or failed, so Wikipedia and trade press were used for those yards. Out-of-definition rows are kept with why_not (repair-only, aluminum-only, fiberglass, closed or not yet built, outside definition). Independence: no ledger file about this vertical was opened. The shared scratchpad pages/ folder held other agents' saved pages. Their file names appeared once in a directory listing; none were opened, and this audit's pages were kept in a separate auditA/ folder.
